groups.title: Authentication Concepts
groups.question: You are adding login to your Rails app, plus an admin role that can delete any recipe. Explain how sessions, password storage and roles work.

followUps.Sessions, cookies, and stateful authenti: How does a Rails session keep a user logged in?
followUps.Authorization roles and permissions desi: How is authorization different from authentication?

evidence.text: Rails stores session data in a signed, encrypted cookie.
The session persists data like the user id between requests.
Signing and encryption stop users from reading or changing it.
It hashes passwords with bcrypt before saving.
bcrypt is deliberately slow and salted, which makes cracking leaked hashes hard.
It adds an authenticate method that checks a password against the hash.
Authentication checks who the user is; authorization decides what they may do.
Roles like admin and user group permissions.
Permissions are checked before sensitive actions.

groups.title: Authentication Patterns
groups.question: You are building sign-up, login and logout by hand, and some pages must only be seen by logged-in users. Explain the flow and how you protect actions.

followUps.User signup, login, and logout flow: Walk through what happens at sign-up, login and logout.
followUps.Protecting controller actions with befor: How does before_action protect controller actions?

evidence.text: Sign-up creates a user with a hashed password.
Login checks credentials and stores the user id in the session.
Logout clears the session.

notEnough: Only saying users can log in and out.

evidence.text: before_action runs a method before chosen actions.
If the user is not logged in, it redirects and stops the action.
It can apply to all actions with exceptions for public ones.

groups.title: Authentication Libraries
groups.question: You need password resets, email confirmation and 'Sign in with GitHub' quickly. Explain the libraries you would use.

followUps.Devise gem for full-featured authenticat: What does Devise give you out of the box?
followUps.OmniAuth for third-party OAuth providers: How does OmniAuth add GitHub login?

evidence.text: Devise provides sign-up, sign-in, password reset and email confirmation.
It is modular, so you enable only the features you need.
It saves time but adds conventions you must learn and customise around.
OmniAuth gives one interface for OAuth providers.
Each provider, like GitHub or Google, is added as a strategy with its credentials.
It integrates with Devise to sign in or create the user.

groups.title: Authorization Libraries
groups.question: Rules like 'only the author or an admin can edit a recipe' are scattered across controllers. Explain how Pundit or CanCanCan organise authorization.

followUps.Pundit policy objects for authorization: How does Pundit structure authorization rules?
followUps.CanCanCan ability-based authorization: How does CanCanCan differ from Pundit?

evidence.text: Pundit uses a plain Ruby policy class per model.
Each action has a method, like update?, returning true or false.
Controllers call authorize, keeping rules out of controllers.
CanCanCan defines all permissions in one Ability class.
Rules are written with can and cannot.
It can load and authorize resources for standard actions automatically.
